text:
I’m here in The bar in my neighborhood to feel … something. That feeling is supposed, I don’t know. Buzzed, maybe. Maybe Tipsy. But alone, they tell me, the best parts of being drunk: relaxation, coexistence, a light yen for human connection. The opportunity to forget, for a moment, the relentless terror of being alive.
I’m not drinking alcohol. Instead, I have science. Specifically, what I have is an ambient temperature taking of a non -alcoholic drink somewhat cloudy called Sentia, which has recently arrived on the US coasts.
I felt Spirits is a “0% ABV alcohol -free botanical drink” that, however, promises a A bit of ooh-la-la —A feeling that its manufacturers expect it to be pleasant enough so that it does not feel the need to support it with a much more risky whiskey taking.
Photography: Matthew Korfhage
Siria’s non -alcoholic beverages do not contain any particular drug. But a single -ounce dose offers a sensation a bit like that first moment you know you have drunk: it is a promise of drunkenness that never arrives. I feel a little confusion in my frontal lobe, a premonition of tingling.
“It is not a buzz, actually,” says one of the multiple waiters who also agreed to try the three flavors of Siria: Gaba Gold, Gaba Red and Gaba Black, in the spirit of scientific research. “It is a lightness. It is the good part of being high without fool. “
Another cantinero, asked to describe the sensation, makes a couple of hand gestures, then believe that he will find words for her later.
In the language of Trek I felt Synthes —A psychoactive drink that theoretically offers less consequences than alcohol and, of course, without hangover.
So how do non -alcoholic beverages put you? And is it pleasant? We have some thoughts, after trying the three flavors of Sentia with the help of some of the best waiters of South Philly.
A scientific pedigree Let’s be clear: products similar to Sent were often the incomplete scope of Bong stores and front windows of the service station, or that hall in a natural food store that always smells like potter’s clay.
But I felt comes with a pedigree. The drink was developed by a neuropsychsypsypsypsycarmacologist quite renowned called David Nutt, a President of Imperial College London Who enjoys a glass of wine on Saturday, but has advised for a long time for solutions to the scourge of alcohol abuse, which CDC causes Around 178,000 deaths In the United States annually, not counting car accidents.
Nutt, who was personally dismissed By the Secretary of the Interior of Great Britain to present evidence that alcohol caused more damage in general than cannabis or LSD, is not trying to prevent people from looking for social lubricants.
